body:
Looks likt it is $primary-color, but I don't see how that fits in to what you have (because the button wouldn't fade to gray, it would fade to a darker blue).

Edit:
$secondary-color: #f0f0f0;

If you reset that before you load the other css files, I wonder if that helps.

Yeah, I think the $secondary-color may be what's off.  I'm going to pull the latest and see if I can reproduce.  I have a base installation for 0.4.3 currently in production mode and I'm not seeing the issue you are seeing. Are you on master or what version of aa are you on?
I'm using c183c89f1c from April 11. I don't see anything in recent commits that would cause this.

I didn't either.  In the past I noticed this once, using firefox or chrome, I saw that one of the files wasn't being included properly.  Can you confirm that all of your compiled css is making it to the browser?

I've seen this in SASS generally when you try to use a mixin for gradients.  I think it happens when you don't put quotes around the colors in the filter declaration - try something like this:

filter: "progid:DXImageTransform.Microsoft.gradient(startColorstr='#{$from}', endColorstr='#{$to}')"

Is the site publicly accessible?  I'd like to see if I can't troubleshoot and see where that color is coming from.

Edit: I guess if it is, probably don't want me messing around in your admin interface... What to do...

Edit: And have you tried this in other browsers?  It does work right in all of those?  Have you tried clearing your local cache in IE to verify you're getting the latest?

In any case, thanks for offering :-)

I'm not entirely sure how to flush the cache in IE, so I've been opening private browsing sessions, deleting everything, and even rebooting. As far as non-mobile browsers, I've tried IE 7/8, Safari, Firefox, and Chrome. It renders just fine in everything but Internet Explorer. What's weird is that 3 weeks ago when I last tried IE, I didn't run into this problem.

Are there any sort of diagnostics/developer tools for IE?
Yes.  It's called Developer Tools.  http://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/dd565622%28v=vs.85%29.aspx

...huh. Turns out @oldtinroof's suggestion worked like a charm.

Selectively turning CSS rules on and off in IE, I discovered that the gradient rules were the problem. This works for the "new" button on the top right of an index page, added in `active_admin.css.scss` (his single quotes aren't needed)

``` sass
#title_bar .action_items A {
  filter: "progid:DXImageTransform.Microsoft.gradient(startColorstr=fff, endColorstr=e7e7e7)"
}
```

When the standard CSS rule IE is getting is as such:

``` css
filter:progid:DXImageTransform.Microsoft.gradient(startColorstr=#fff, endColorstr=#e7e7e7); BORDER-LEFT: #c7c7c7 1px solid
```

So now that I've found a solution, the question becomes: what's causing this to show up now? Has anyone run into this using ActiveAdmin?
I can see where the problem is in the gradients mixin in the source.  I'll try and sort it and put a pull request in this afternoon.

^^^ The double-quote escaping is less than graceful, but it works.
edit: never mind, only a single set of quotes was necessary after all: 7d75988e9f192defd2be10a353aa2f989a4043f8
Great, glad that worked for you Daxter!

body: Thank you.

I merged this and pointed it at a production like environment and see blue buttons now.  After I reverted it on https://github.com/jancel/active_admin/tree/blue_buttons, my blue buttons in active_admin went away.  This must be an environment issue; I'm running debian and precompiling my assets with a script, not using default precompiles.

If you point gem 'activeadmin', :git => "git://github.com/jancel/active_admin.git", :branch => "blue_buttons"

I'm assuming you'll see the blue buttons again.  I'm wondering if this is SASS or IE.  I'm leaning towards SASS.  

I'm going to do some more research, and see if I can't track down your specific cause here.  It may not be IE.

@Daxter can you try my branch and see if it fixes your issue (with blue buttons)?  I have made a change that I found on the sass site, and thinking it may be related.  In your gemfile,

gem 'activeadmin', :git => "git://github.com/jancel/active_admin.git", :branch => "blue_buttons"

I actually just did, expecting to see blue buttons, but all was fine. Only now did I see your second post. Your fix worked. :)

Now why would my fix work for me, but not for you? I'm using RVM on RHEL, and I use the default precompile. How exactly do you script the precompiling?
I'm using RVM, Capistrano, on Debian Linux.  I precompile using this gist: https://gist.github.com/2483107
